transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (AtlasHealth ML Eng), Liam (Infra), Sofia (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):
- Reviewed TTFT regressions since switching to fused-attn kernel on v2 runner; noticeable p99 spikes on longer sequences and streaming handshakes.
- Decided on A/B kernel run (flash vs fused) with seq_len 512 and 1024, capture per-token and handshake latencies; Redwood to share security docs and Atlas to provide representative traces.

Topics: TTFT numbers, streaming handshake variance, sequence length distribution, kernel selection, security/SSO/KMS, next steps for pilot decision.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: All right everyone, thanks for joining. I'll do a quick roll call, uh, and then Ethan will walk through the recent TTFT runs.
[00:08] Priya: Hey Maya, hi Ethan. Priya here.
[00:09] Liam: Liam on infra.
[00:10] Sofia: Sofia for product.
[00:11] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood. Good morning.
[00:13] Maya: Cool. Quick goal for today — we want to triage that p99 spike you saw in the last three days, figure out whether it's kernel, sequence length distribution, or streaming handshake, and set the bench plan.
[00:24] Priya: Yeah, thanks. We started seeing that after you rolled the fused-attn kernel default — median TTFT improved but p99 went up, especially when sequence length crosses ~700 tokens. Streaming sessions also had a higher tail — some customers saw 600–900ms first token.
[00:39] Ethan: Right, so short summary from our side: fused-attn gives better avg throughput on typical seq 256 loads but it exposes a slow path for long sequences and when KV cache warming happens in streaming. We suspect kernel fallback and cache eviction interplay.
[00:51] Liam: To be clear — our requests are mixed. About 70% are short (<=256), 25% mid (257–768), 5% long (>768). So p99 is dominated by those long ones but they are business-critical (long patient notes generation).
[01:05] Maya: Thanks. Priya, did you say the long ones are like medical note generation — so they can't be truncated?
[01:11] Priya: Right. We can chunk but it changes project quality; they'd prefer single-pass where possible.
[01:16] Ethan: Ok. A couple of quick data points from our test cluster: when we ran fused-attn at seq_len 1024, TTFT median was 140ms, p95 360ms, p99 820ms. With flash-attn variant, median 160ms, p95 300ms, p99 420ms. So flash seems to reduce extreme tail at cost of a slightly higher median in this run.
[01:35] Maya: Hmm that's interesting — fused better median but worse tail. We need to make decision around tradeoff for AtlasHealth workload.
[01:42] Sofia: For product decisions, we care more about 95/99 since clinicians see those slow responses. Slightly higher median is okay.
[01:48] Ethan: Understood. There's also the streaming handshake overhead — our streaming path does an initial KV warm and small handshake exchange; if client RTTs vary or there's an early small token back-and-forth it amplifies.
[02:00] Priya: We do have some mobile clients with higher RTT that start streaming then switch to background requests. That probably explains some of the variance.
[02:06] Liam: On infra — we've pinned experiments to g5-like instances in our test; we plan to try Dedicated Redwood nodes eventually, but right now it's more of an apples-to-apples on our side.
[02:16] Maya: Good. A couple of tactical items: Ethan, can you run a controlled A/B with the two kernels, across seq_lens 256/512/1024, batch sizes 1 and 4, and include streaming handshake times? Also capture cold vs warm KV cache runs.
[02:31] Ethan: Yep, we'll script that. For cold vs warm, we can run a short warmup and then sample; for cold we can purge and run. Expect CSV with columns: seq_len, kernel, batch, median_TTFT, p95, p99, handshake_mean.
[02:44] Priya: And include percent of samples that hit the fallback path — sometimes the runtime introspects and changes kernel mid-stream which shows up as step-jumps.
[02:51] Ethan: Good point — we'll log kernel switch events.
[02:53] Sofia: From product side, we also want a view on tokenization differences and whether our longer notes have heavy prefix repetition that could be cached.
[03:03] Priya: There is prefix repetition— templates and boilerplate — but the clinical sections vary. Caching could help but needs careful invalidation.
[03:10] Maya: On security — Atlas asked about KMS integration and SSO steps last week. I said we'd send the brief pack. We'll include how keys are wrapped, audit logs retention, and the onboarding SAML flow.
[03:21] Priya: Perfect. Also compliance: SOC2 type II is a must — any gaps around VPC peering or audit log export?
[03:27] Maya: Redwood has SOC2; we'll include the report. For VPC, we can do private deployment or VPC peering depending on your needs; audit logs can stream to your SIEM via our log export. We'll detail retention options.
[03:39] Liam: On the network front, can you confirm egress rules during benchmarks? We need to know which IP ranges for the test nodes.
[03:45] Ethan: Yep, we'll provide ephemeral IPs for the bench run and a CIDR for the VPC instructions.
[03:49] Priya: Back to latency — what's the impact of quantization on these kernels? We tried q4hf in dev and saw a small accuracy delta but big perf wins, but worried about p99 interactions.
[03:59] Ethan: Quantization tends to compress compute but kernel implementations vary. Some kernels have optimized int8 paths that lower median and tail; others degrade tail slightly due to dequant overhead on streaming. We'll include quantized runs as an optional appendix if you want.
[04:13] Maya: Priya — is Atlas open to a short tradeoff: enable flash-attn for long sequences and fused for short? We could route by policy.
[04:20] Priya: That could work if the routing latency is negligible. Does Redwood support per-request routing policy based on seq_len?
[04:27] Ethan: Yes, we can route by policy. The routing cost is microseconds; the bigger work is ensuring the model variant is compatible. For this POC we'd probably route to the same model but different kernel parameter at runtime.
[04:39] Mia? [background]* (crosstalk)
[04:40] Sofia: Sorry — typo, ignore.
[04:42] Liam: One question on cost — do we have estimates for token cost delta when moving to flash-attn? Not just compute but also egress/nodes sizing.
[04:51] Maya: We can estimate; Ethan can produce relative compute cycles and we can translate to cost per 1M tokens for pilot config.
[04:58] Ethan: I can give a rough cost delta after the A/B run; will include node utilization and expected throughput.
[05:03] Priya: Ok next — instrumentation. We need the logs to show both per-token emit times and kernel switch markers. Can Redwood attach unique request IDs back into our headers?
[05:12] Ethan: Yes, we support request_id propagation. We'll surface it in the bench CSV and in traces.
[05:18] Maya: Great. Any blockers to running the A/B this week?
[05:21] Priya: Not from us. We'll generate the 48h trace for you and spin up a test VPC next week.
[05:26] Liam: We'll also open a ticket with our security folks once we get the SOC2 pack.
[05:29] Maya: Cool. Before we wrap, quick recap and owners.

Recap:
- Run A/B kernel experiment (Ethan) capturing TTFT median/p95/p99, streaming handshake, kernel-switch events, quantized appendix if feasible.
- Atlas to provide 48h request traces and provision ephemeral VPC for bench.
- Redwood to send security pack + SSO/KMS notes and a cost sketch.

[05:48] Sofia: One last tiny ask — if you have a recommended starter config for streaming (batching/window size/handshake threshold) send that too; we'd prefer a plug-and-play suggestion.
[05:58] Ethan: Will include a recommended streaming profile: handshake window 64ms, prefetch KV for seq>512, batching target 1–2 for low-latency.
[06:06] Priya: Great thanks.
[06:07] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and the CSV link. Speak next week.
[06:12] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings present (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache), punctuation trimmed; speaker labels occasionally simplified.
